newsitem.title: USA: U.S. transport plane, with 11 aboard, crashes.
newsitem.headline: U.S. transport plane, with 11 aboard, crashes.

text.p: A U.S. Air Force Reserve transport plane with 11 people on board crashed into the Pacific Ocean off the northern California coast on Friday, officials said.
One survivor was rescued in critical condition, but the fate of the other 10 people on board was not immediately known, the Coast Guard said.

The Air Force said the HC-130 Hercules crashed on Friday evening while flying from Portland Air Base to San Diego, California, on a routine training mission. It said 11 people were on board the aircraft, which was based in Portland, Oregon, and assigned to the 939th Rescue Wing's 304th Rescue Squadron.
Coast Guard planes and boats from several California bases rushed to the crash site, about 60 miles (95 km) west of Cape Mendocino on the northern California coast.
The Coast Guard said a helicopter rescued one survivor in critical condition who was being treated at a California hospital, but had not located anyone else.
"We'll keep searching through the night," Coast Guard spokeswoman Shelly Freier said.
She had no information on weather conditions, but said the darkness so far out at sea would make it difficult to find survivors.
Another Coast Guard spokesman, Jeff Murphy, said the C-130 reported an electrical failure, and some time afterward a Seattle communications centre lost radio contact with the plane.

Murphy said the Coast Guard sent a C-130 and two helicopters to the crash site to search for survivors. A Coast Guard search and rescue ship was on its way to the area and another helicopter would be leaving soon, he said.
The Air Force said crew members' names were being withheld pending notification of their families.
There was no immediate word on what might have caused the crash.
